newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan liquid reserves rise to $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan liquid reserves rise to $1 billion.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Thursday foreign exchange reserves, excluding bullion, had risen to $1.068 billion from $850 million on February 20.
The SBP, in a statement issued after a board meeting in Lahore, appealed to all Pakistanis at home and abroad to respond to Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's debt retirement plan.
Sharif has asked Pakistanis to give or deposit money in special government accounts to help pay off their country's $30 billion foreign debt.
An SBP official said remittances from Pakistani expatriates had picked up since Sharif made his appeal on Monday.

Bankers said this month's $150 million five-year convertible bond issue by state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd and a $115.5 million short-term financing facility arranged by foreign banks for the same company may have contributed to the rise in reserves, which stood at $1.546 billion on February 22, 1996.
